attachments.name: medical_plan.txt
attachments.text:
EVENT MEDICAL PLAN
Marina Tri City Race 10K, Saturday 13 March 2027
Applicant: Marina Tri Club
Issue: 1.2

1. Event summary
A 10K race with 80 runners, starting at 08:00 in the Millbank Quarter area of Port Halden. An ambulance from Sentinel Ambulance Service is on site for the race; the paperwork is attached.

2. First aid cover
3 first aid posts will operate, at the start, at the finish and at the course midpoint, staffed by 8 qualified first aiders. Posts are placed so that no part of the course is more than 1.5 km from one. Two cycle responders move along the course with defibrillators.

3. Weather and hydration
Participants are reminded in their pre-race information to dress appropriately for the conditions and to drink plenty of fluids before, during and after the race. Our experienced committee will keep a close eye on the weather in the days leading up to the event.

4. Transfer to hospital
The receiving hospital is Thornton County Hospital, 16 km from the finish. The transfer route and the pick-up point at the top of Albion Road have been walked with the first aid team. The hospital's emergency department has been told the date and the expected numbers.

Some background. Our committee has run this race for a number of years and takes the welfare of runners to heart. One of our longtime members is a retired paramedic who usually runs the race herself and is not on duty that day.

5. Communications
Members of the team will have their mobile phones with them, and a list of contact numbers will be circulated in the week before the event. Coverage in the area is generally reported to be good.

6. Clinical lead
Responsibility for welfare on the day rests with the race director, supported by the wider committee, all of whom take the wellbeing of participants extremely seriously.

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
Marina Tri City Race 10K: how the race will work

Prepared by Owen Cartwright (Race Director), Marina Tri Club. Last updated 11 December 2026.

This is our plan for race day, Saturday 13 March 2027. We expect 80 runners over 10K (10 km). Numbers can be collected from the top of Albion Road from an hour before we go at 08:00, and we aim to have the last finisher home by 10:00.

The route takes in Albion Road, Dyer Street and Rope Walk, and the City would need to close all of these for us. On the way round we cross none. We finish in the Civic Plaza.

There's plenty of room. Albion Road is about 16 metres across, Dyer Street about 14 metres and Rope Walk about 9 metres, and all have broad pavements too. We line up across the full width of Albion Road, and the finish opens out into the Civic Plaza, where there's space for everyone.

Our club has put on races for some years now and we keep to the same simple format: chip timing, water on the course, and a hot drink at the end. Results go up on our website the same evening.

attachments.name: traffic_plan.txt
attachments.text:
TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN
Event: Marina Tri City Race 10K
Date: Saturday 13 March 2027
Applicant: Marina Tri Club
Prepared by: Halloway Road Management
Issue: 1.2

1. Scope
This plan describes how traffic will be managed for the Marina Tri City Race 10K, a 10K race in the Millbank Quarter area of Port Halden with a 08:00 start. It has been prepared to accompany the permit application and should be read with the race plan. See the attached correspondence from the police for the escort.

2. Road closures
Temporary closures will be in force as follows, with barriers and advance signing supplied by Signal Hill Traffic Services.
- Albion Road, Hatter Street to Salter Way: closed 07:00 to 10:30
- Dyer Street, Brook Street to Hatter Street: closed 07:00 to 10:30
- Rope Walk, Tanner Street to Salter Way: closed 07:00 to 10:30

3. Major crossings
The course does not cross any major road, so no separate crossing control is proposed.

4. Diversions
Drivers will be advised to expect delays in the area and to allow additional time for their journeys. Advance information boards will be used where practical, and through traffic is expected to find alternative routes across the wider network.

5. Emergency vehicle access
The emergency services will be made aware of the event date and general location through the usual channels ahead of the day. Any vehicle attending an incident will be accommodated by staff on the ground as circumstances allow.

6. Notification
All frontages on the closed streets receive a letter drop 21 days before the event, with a further reminder at 7 days. Advance notice signs go up 10 days before, and bus operators have been given the closure times.

7. Reopening
Roads will be reopened following the conclusion of the event, once barriers and equipment have been removed by the contractor.
